title: 1978 AHSME Problem 18
statement: What is the smallest positive integer \(n\) such that \(\sqrt n-\sqrt{n-1}\lt0.01?\)

solutions.text:
Rationalizing gives \[ \sqrt n-\sqrt{n-1} =\frac1{\sqrt n+\sqrt{n-1}}. \] For \(n=2500,\) the denominator is \(50+\sqrt{2499}\lt100,\) so the difference exceeds \(0.01.\) For \(n=2501,\) the denominator is \(\sqrt{2501}+50\gt100,\) so the difference is less than \(0.01.\) The denominator increases with \(n,\) making \(2501\) the least such integer.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Compare the resulting denominator with \(100\) near \(n=2500\)
